s0007: Market grows in value, but with important shifts
s0021: The pharma market is growing in value, but unit demand is falling. In 2026 the category is getting pricier: the average pack price rises to **RUB 432.5** (+14.8% vs January–August 2025). The average pharmacy purchase in Russia across the full range (incl. drugs and parapharmaceuticals) reached **RUB 888.5** in August 2026 (+15% vs August 2025).
s0023: Prescription drugs are the main growth engine: they grow in value and make up most of the market’s turnover. The OTC segment, by contrast, faces falling demand. High-cost drugs are reshaping the market fast: Tirzepta sales topped **RUB 15.9 bn** in six months, and Sedjaro grew **87-fold**.
s0026: The big screen is going digital, like the pharmacy shelf
s0032: most often see drug ads on Smart TV/CTV
s0035: Linear TV still holds a key place in pharma’s media mix, but the big screen itself is changing fast. Viewers increasingly watch via Smart TV and CTV, and ad money follows them: PHD estimates Russia’s DTV market could grow **from RUB 6 bn to 15 bn** in 2026. Pharma is already among the segment’s biggest advertisers, with share of voice reaching **about 18%** in Q1.
s0036: Online sales and reservations of pharmacy products are growing almost three times faster than total pharmacy revenue in Russia: **+28.8% vs +9.7%** in H1 2026. ePharma already holds **28.2%** of the market, up from 24% a year earlier. 4% of drug buyers use the online channel, and one in five buys medicines only online.
